title: Underline ignores its color
body:
### Summary

Underline ignores its color and uses the color of a word.

### Reproduction Steps

<!-- Ideally provide a key sequence and/or asciinema.org recording. --> 

I tried this:

In `mytheme.toml`:
```toml
"diagnostic.error" = { fg = "blue", underline = { color = "red", style = "curl"} }
```
I expected this to happen:
The color of the underline is red, the color of the word is blue

Instead, this happened:
The color of the underline is blue and the color of the word is also blue
![image](https://github.com/helix-editor/helix/assets/61053971/acaa3eee-4ba7-404d-b7bd-ef9098091c21)


### Helix log

_No response_

### Platform

Windows

### Terminal Emulator

Windows Terminal, Alacritty

### Helix Version

helix 23.05 (7f5940be)

comments.author: participant1
comments.body:
Can you try setting

```
[editor]
undercurl = true
```

To force undercurl it seems that the curly underline isn't showing up at all

comments.author: participant1
comments.body:
> In config.toml:

theme changes need to be done in a theme file, see making a theme https://<redacted-host>/themes.html#creating-a-theme

you can use ``inherits = "<theme you want to change>"`` in that file to override the underline of a specific theme

comments.body: @participant1 Oh, I meant to write `mytheme.toml` not `config.toml`. I'm going to edit the description.

comments.author: participant2
comments.body: I was unable to reproduce, tried on Alacritty but I got the expected results.

comments.author: participant3
comments.body: If I remember correctly this is a Windows thing. The underline colors and styles get ignored (and filtered out) by conpty, so there's nothing that helix or even the terminal emulator can do.

comments.author: participant1
comments.body: That makes sense that it is a terminal issue, if it is not you should be able see the curly underline on most themes, cause almost all of them use it

comments.author: participant1
comments.body: This also affects alacritty on windows, so it can probably be marked as upstream and closed

comments.author: participant6
comments.body:
Interestingly I have the issue on Linux with Alacrity using tmux i.e. the undercurl color is derived from syntax highlighting instead of the predefined `red`. The color is accurate (`red`) if I am not inside tmux. I did verify that this is not due to some environment variable by syncing the env variables in both non-tmux and tmux session.

Also I have tried setting `undercurl` in config to no help.

comments.author: participant6
comments.body:
Update: I was able to get undercurl color working correctly on tmux by following suggestion at: https://<redacted-host>/r/neovim/comments/vqbu8m/undercurl_support_on_different_terminals/ieoxghg/

Specifically enabling coloring by adding following to `~/.tmux.conf`
```
set -as terminal-overrides ',*:Smulx=\E[4::%p1%dm'  # undercurl support
set -as terminal-overrides ',*:Setulc=\E[58::2::%p1%{65536}%/%d::%p1%{256}%/%{255}%&%d::%p1%{255}%&%d%;m'  # underscore colors - needs tmux-3.0
```
